author: A grateful patron of the Drowsy Elk inn
pages:
#Ode to Honey Mead

~O golden friend in a wooden cup,
~sweet sunlight of the bees,
~you lift a weary traveller up
~and warm him to the knees.

~You made the shy man sing aloud,
~the sad man laugh till dawn,
~and made the quiet jarl so proud
~he danced upon the lawn.

~You made my brother wrestle bears
~(he lost, but bravely so);
~you made my uncle climb the stairs
~that lead to nowhere. Oh.

~Yet in the morning, cruel friend,
~you hammer at my head;
~I swear an oath that all must end,
~and lie quite still in bed.

~But then the evening comes again,
~the firelight, the song,
~and someone says "Just one, and then..."
~and so I play along.

#A Note from the Innkeeper

The author of this poem owes the Drowsy Elk eleven gold and one table. We have kept the poem as a deposit.
